boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named Kettering spaces where students can study, build, eat, exercise, cook, compete and gather, verified through current university sources.

cards.title: Take Your Study Session to the Roof
cards.subtitle: Outdoor work space at the Learning Commons
cards.notes: Bring charged devices and use the terrace’s outlets, shaded seating and hammocks for an outdoor reading or project session.
cards.short_summary: A 1,600-square-foot rooftop study area with seating, greenery, hammocks and electrical outlets.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering identifies the Rooftop Terrace as a 1,600-square-foot Learning Commons space with seating, green areas, hammocks and electrical outlets for working outdoors.
cards.access_notes: Access is tied to the Learning Commons; the university page does not publish separate terrace hours or public-access terms.

cards.title: Start Research at the Knowledge Bar
cards.subtitle: Library help and digital resources in the Learning Commons
cards.notes: Begin a research session here when you need library assistance, then continue with the digital collection from elsewhere on campus.
cards.short_summary: The Learning Commons base for library service and access to Kettering’s extensive digital collections.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering says its Knowledge Bars host the digital library, which includes more than 900,000 e-books, 100,000 e-journals and over 100 databases.
cards.access_notes: In-person use follows Learning Commons access; Kettering students and faculty can use the digital library beyond this physical space.

cards.title: Turn a Design Into a Physical Prototype
cards.subtitle: Hands-on fabrication space in the Learning Commons
cards.notes: Arrive with a defined prototype task and confirm the required training before using the design stations, soldering gear or 3-D printers.
cards.short_summary: A 15,000-square-foot fabrication environment for testing designs with specialized tools.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering describes its 15,000-square-foot Makerspace as providing 3-D printers, design stations, soldering equipment and other prototyping tools.
cards.access_notes: The source does not state public hours, eligibility rules or required training; verify access and equipment procedures before visiting.

cards.title: Settle In for a Group Meal
cards.subtitle: First-floor dining in the Learning Commons
cards.notes: Use the café seating for a meal with classmates, and check the current dining-hours page before planning around a particular service period.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor campus café designed for both quick food pickup and meals with friends.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering places Battenberg Café on the Learning Commons first floor and says students may grab food to go or sit for a meal with friends across eight food stations.
cards.access_notes: Food service follows posted dining periods; purchases require a meal plan, dining funds or another accepted payment method.

cards.entity_name: Great Lakes Coffee Shop - BorgWarner Bistro
cards.title: Meet Above the Main Café
cards.subtitle: Second-floor coffee shop in the Learning Commons
cards.notes: Choose this second-floor counter for a short classmate meetup, then carry the conversation into nearby Learning Commons seating.
cards.short_summary: An upstairs coffee counter serving locally roasted drinks and pastries beside shared campus seating.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering identifies Great Lakes Coffee Shop on the Learning Commons second floor and says it serves locally roasted coffee, other beverages and pastries.
cards.access_notes: The current university hours page lists weekday service and weekend closure; consult it before visiting because schedules may change.

cards.title: Move Between Courts, Track and Pool
cards.subtitle: Kettering’s student recreation facility
cards.notes: Check the separate facility and pool schedules, then choose among the track, courts, fitness rooms or six-lane swimming pool.
cards.short_summary: A 70,000-square-foot recreation center combining fitness, aquatic, court and lounge facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering says the center contains a six-lane pool, four basketball courts, four racquetball courts, a suspended track, fitness areas and student lounges.
cards.access_notes: This is a private facility for Kettering faculty, staff, students and their family members; community use requires a reservation.

cards.title: Cook Beyond the Microfridge
cards.subtitle: Shared second-floor kitchen for Thompson Hall residents
cards.notes: Coordinate ingredients and cleanup with hallmates, then use the second-floor kitchen when a residence-room microfridge is not enough.
cards.short_summary: A shared residence-hall kitchen that gives Thompson Hall students a place to prepare meals.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering states that Thompson Hall’s Community Kitchen is on the second floor and is available for residents to prepare meals at their convenience.
cards.access_notes: The kitchen is presented as a Thompson Hall amenity; residence access controls and kitchen rules apply.

cards.title: Build Where Full-Size Robots Practice
cards.subtitle: Robotics build and practice facility beside the Academic Building
cards.notes: Connect through an affiliated robotics program before bringing a build; the center supports machining, printing and regulation-field testing.
cards.short_summary: A dedicated robotics facility serving land-based, aerial, FIRST and VEX programs.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering says the Robotics Center supports several robotics programs and provides resources including build areas, a regulation-size practice field, machining labs and 3-D printers.
cards.access_notes: Use is program-based; the university page does not advertise unrestricted drop-in access or general public hours.

cards.title: Build With a Competition Team
cards.subtitle: Vehicle-project space in the C.S. Mott Engineering and Science Center
cards.notes: Join the appropriate competition team and follow shop procedures before using this project space to develop or service a student vehicle.
cards.short_summary: A hands-on vehicle design space supporting Kettering’s student engineering teams.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering lists the SAE Design Center among its mechanical-engineering labs and says Formula SAE students design and race a formula car in competition.
cards.access_notes: This is an instructional and competition-team facility, not an unrestricted public workspace; team and laboratory procedures apply.

cards.title: Take Intramurals Into the Stadium
cards.subtitle: Shared athletics and community venue in Carriage Town
cards.notes: Watch the recreation schedule for student field use, and follow event-specific entry rules when the stadium hosts ceremonies or community programs.
cards.short_summary: An 11,000-seat university-owned stadium shared by intramurals, local teams and community events.
cards.evidence_claim: Kettering states that its intramural and recreational sports programs use Atwood Stadium, which also hosts school athletics and community gatherings.
cards.access_notes: Access depends on scheduled recreation, athletics or public events; some events, including commencement, require tickets.

warnings: Exact coordinates and verified Google Maps destination URLs were not available from the cited university pages, so those fields are null.
